title: Model families and types
subtitle: I pick a model for the job and the hardware it has to run on, then I change it until it fits.

lede: Depending on the job, I fine-tune a model, quantize it, convert it, build an inference engine for it, or measure it against alternatives. The work spans most of the model families in use today. My Capabilities model is a dense model of about half a billion parameters, fully fine-tuned so that a tool catalog lives in its weights. I trained a ladder of small dense models at sub-billion, half-billion and low-billion sizes, and chose the size from measured recall and training time. A half-billion-parameter model became a tool index because a full fine-tune takes minutes. I try the standard runtime first.
quote: I size the model to the problem.
evidence: LLM quantization (FP8 and 4-bit): 4-bit and mixed 4-bit/FP8 builds of a 27B-class hybrid model on one 32 GB card, the all-4-bit build +36% throughput at +3.3% perplexity.
Model selection across families: dense, mixture-of-experts at 3B of 30B active, hybrid recurrent-attention, embedding, speech and diffusion models from <1B to 70B+ parameters.
Inference serving architecture: runtimes chosen per hardware and job, TensorRT-LLM and my own CUDA engine on NVIDIA, vLLM's XPU build and OpenVINO on Intel.
author: Corey James
